root_cause.text: During kexec, the `load_segments()` function invalidates the GS base register, causing subsequent KCOV-instrumented C code in `machine_kexec_64.c` and `physaddr.c` to crash when attempting to access per-CPU data.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "The load_segments() function changes segment registers, invalidating GS base (which KCOV relies on for per-cpu data). When CONFIG_KCOV is enabled, any subsequent instrumented C code call (e.g. native_gdt_invalidate()) begins crashing the kernel in an endless loop," which is resolved in the patch by setting `KCOV_INSTRUMENT_machine_kexec_64.o := n` and `KCOV_INSTRUMENT_physaddr.o := n`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for machine_kexec_64.o to prevent crashes during kexec when the GS base is invalidated.
intent_record.what: Added KCOV_INSTRUMENT_machine_kexec_64.o := n to the Makefile, disabling KCOV instrumentation for that object file.
intent_record.how: This prevents kernel crashes during kexec operations by ensuring KCOV does not attempt to access per-CPU data via the GS base after it has been invalidated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for physaddr.o to prevent instrumentation-induced failures during early physical address translation.
intent_record.what: Added KCOV_INSTRUMENT_physaddr.o := n to disable KCOV instrumentation for physaddr.o, accompanied by an explanatory comment.
intent_record.how: Disables runtime coverage tracking for physical address calculation code, preventing potential recursion or boot-time crashes in early memory management.
